The F3Set framework addresses fast, frequent, and fine-grained event detection through a hierarchical decomposition of events into sub-classes. Each event is represented as a combination of 8 sub-classes, yielding up to 1,108 distinct types. The system uses a multi-label classifier to predict event elements rather than discrete classes, mitigating combinatorial explosion. The core innovation lies in the F3ED architecture, which employs a video encoder with Temporal Shift Modules (TSM) and a bidirectional GRU for contextual refinement. The event localizer performs binary classification per frame using sigmoid activation and BCE loss. The multi-label classifier operates on frame-level features to produce event vectors. Contextual refinement enhances predictions by leveraging temporal dependencies. The system achieves high performance at all granularity levels, especially with BiGRU-based context modeling. This structure allows for precise temporal alignment within ±1 frame, enabling detailed analysis of rapid sequences such as tennis rallies. The modular design supports extension to other domains like NFL play phases, where frame-precise event tracking is crucial.
